samples.gvd:
module pe (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [31:0] a,
    input [31:0] b,
    output reg [31:0] c
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) c <= 32'b0; else c <= c + (a * b);
    end

endmodule

    <description>Parallel Multiplier-Accumulator (MAC) for 32-bit integers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operations.</input>

        <input id="a" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit input operand A.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit input operand B.</input>
        <output id="c" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit output representing the accumulated result.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>Performs parallel multiplication and accumulation of 32-bit inputs.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="sub_64bit">
    <description>64-bit Subtractor with Overflow Checking</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[63:0]">First 64-bit input operand.</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[63:0]">Second 64-bit input operand.</input>
        <output id="result" width_description="[63:0]">64-bit output representing the difference of the two operands.</output>
        <output id="overflow">1-bit output indicating whether an overflow occurred during the subtraction operation.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Perform 64-bit subtraction
        assign result = A - B;
        
        // Detect overflow
        assign overflow = ((A[63] == 0 && B[63] == 1 && result[63] == 1) || 
                          (A[63] == 1 && B[63] == 0 && result[63] == 0));
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_8bit">
    <description>8-bit multiplier using shift-and-add method.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[7:0]">First 8-bit input operand (multiplicand).</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[7:0]">Second 8-bit input operand (multiplier).</input>
        <output id="product" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit output representing the product of A and B.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Initialize product to 0
        product = 16'b0;
        
        // Iterate over each bit of the multiplier B
        for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) {
            // If the current bit of B is 1, add the multiplicand A shifted left by i positions to the product
            if (B[i] == 1'b1) {
                product = product + (A << i);
            }
        }
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="fixed_point_adder">
    <description>Parameterized fixed-point adder for arithmetic operations with fixed precision.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[N-1:0]">First N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[N-1:0]">Second N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <output id="c" width_description="[N-1:0]">N-bit output representing the result of the fixed-point addition.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="Q">Number of fractional bits (precision).</parameter>
        <parameter id="N">Total number of bits, including integer and fractional parts.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <signal id="res" width_description="[N-1:0]" type="wire">N-bit register used to store the result of the addition or subtraction.</signal>
        <assign>
            if (a[N-1] == b[N-1]) begin
                // Both numbers have the same sign
                res = a + b;
            end else begin
                // Numbers have opposite signs
                if (a >= b) begin
                    res = a - b;
                end else begin
                    res = b - a;
                end
            end
        </assign>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Performs fixed-point addition based on the signs of the inputs.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="width_8to16">
    <description>Data width conversion circuit that converts 8-bit data input to 16-bit data output.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="valid_in">Input signal indicating the validity of the input data.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input data to be converted.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Output signal indicating the validity of the output data.</output>
        <output id="data_out" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit output data resulting from the width conversion.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">Idle state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="WAIT_DATA">Waiting for the second data input.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="data_lock" width_description="[7:0]" type="register">Register to store the first valid data.</reg>
        <reg id="data_out_reg" width_description="[15:0]" type="register">Register to store the 16-bit output data.</reg>
        <reg id="flag" type="register">Flag to indicate if the first valid data has been received.</reg>
        <wire id="next_flag" type="wire">Next value of the flag.</wire>
        <wire id="next_data_out_reg" width_description="[15:0]" type="wire">Next value of the data_out_reg.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                data_out_reg <= 16'b0;
                data_lock <= 8'b0;
                flag <= 1'b0;
                valid_out <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (valid_in && !flag) begin
                    data_lock <= data_in;
                    flag <= 1'b1;
                end else if (valid_in && flag) begin
                    next_data_out_reg <= {data_lock, data_in};
                    data_out_reg <= next_data_out_reg;
                    flag <= 1'b0;
                    valid_out <= 1'b1;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_16bit">
    <description>Unsigned 16-bit multiplier using shift and accumulate operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Chip clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="start">Start signal to initiate multiplication.</input>
        <input id="ain" width_description="[15:0]">Multiplicand input.</input>
        <input id="bin" width_description="[15:0]">Multiplier input.</input>
        <output id="yout" width_description="[31:0]">Product output.</output>
        <output id="done">Completion flag.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH_A" value="16">Width of multiplicand.</parameter>
        <parameter id="WIDTH_B" value="16">Width of multiplier.</parameter>
        <parameter id="WIDTH_Y" value="32">Width of product.</parameter>
        <parameter id="MAX_SHIFT" value="16">Maximum shift count.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="i" width="5">Shift count register.</register>
        <register id="areg" width="16">Multiplicand register.</register>
        <register id="breg" width="16">Multiplier register.</register>
        <register id="yout_r" width="32">Product register.</register>
        <register id="done_r" width="1">Completion flag register.</register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                i <= 5'd0;
                areg <= 16'd0;
                breg <= 16'd0;
                yout_r <= 32'd0;
                done_r <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (start) begin
                    if (i == 5'd0) begin
                        areg <= ain;
                        breg <= bin;
                    end else if (i < 5'd17) begin
                        if (areg[i-1]) begin
                            yout_r <= yout_r + (breg << (i-1));
                        end
                    end
                    i <= i + 5'd1;
                end else begin
                    i <= 5'd0;
                end
                if (i == 5'd16) begin
                    done_r <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    done_r <= 1'b0;
                end
            end
        end
        assign yout = yout_r;
        assign done = done_r;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="edge_detect">
    <description>Detects rising and falling edges in the input signal a and generates corresponding output signals rise and down.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="a">Input signal.</input>
        <output id="rise">Output signal indicating a rising edge.</output>
        <output id="down">Output signal indicating a falling edge.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter>RISING</parameter>
        <parameter>FALLING</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="a_prev" width_description="1">Previous value of input signal a.</reg>
        <reg id="rise_reg" width_description="1">Register for storing the rising edge signal.</reg>
        <reg id="down_reg" width_description="1">Register for storing the falling edge signal.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                a_prev <= 0;
                rise_reg <= 0;
                down_reg <= 0;
            end else begin
                a_prev <= a;
                if (a_prev == 0 && a == 1) begin
                    rise_reg <= 1;
                    down_reg <= 0;
                end else if (a_prev == 1 && a == 0) begin
                    rise_reg <= 0;
                    down_reg <= 1;
                end else begin
                    rise_reg <= 0;
                    down_reg <= 0;
                end
            end
        end
        assign rise = rise_reg;
        assign down = down_reg;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="freq_div">
    <description>Frequency divider for generating 50MHz, 10MHz, and 1MHz clocks from a 100MHz input clock.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="CLK_in">Input clock signal.</input>
        <input id="RST">Reset signal.</input>
        <output id="CLK_50">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 2.</output>
        <output id="CLK_10">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 10.</output>
        <output id="CLK_1">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 100.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="COUNTER_50">50</parameter>
        <parameter id="COUNTER_10">10</parameter>
        <parameter id="COUNTER_1">100</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt_50" width="6">Counter for 50MHz division.</reg>
        <reg id="cnt_10" width="4">Counter for 10MHz division.</reg>
        <reg id="cnt_100" width="7">Counter for 1MHz division.</reg>
        <wire id="CLK_50_reg">Register for CLK_50 output.</wire>
        <wire id="CLK_10_reg">Register for CLK_10 output.</wire>
        <wire id="CLK_1_reg">Register for CLK_1 output.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge CLK_in or negedge RST) begin
            if (!RST) begin
                cnt_50 <= 6'd0;
                cnt_10 <= 4'd0;
                cnt_100 <= 7'd0;
                CLK_50_reg <= 1'b0;
                CLK_10_reg <= 1'b0;
                CLK_1_reg <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                cnt_50 <= cnt_50 + 1;
                if (cnt_50 == COUNTER_50) begin
                    CLK_50_reg <= ~CLK_50_reg;
                    cnt_50 <= 6'd0;
                end

                cnt_10 <= cnt_10 + 1;
                if (cnt_10 == COUNTER_10) begin
                    CLK_10_reg <= ~CLK_10_reg;
                    cnt_10 <= 4'd0;
                end

                cnt_100 <= cnt_100 + 1;
                if (cnt_100 == COUNTER_1) begin
                    CLK_1_reg <= ~CLK_1_reg;
                    cnt_100 <= 7'd0;
                end
            end
        end
        CLK_50 <= CLK_50_reg;
        CLK_10 <= CLK_10_reg;
        CLK_1 <= CLK_1_reg;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="fixed_point_subtractor">
    <description>Fixed-point subtractor for precise arithmetic operations with fixed precision.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[N-1:0]">First N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[N-1:0]">Second N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <output id="c" width_description="[N-1:0]">N-bit output representing the result of the fixed-point subtraction.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="Q">Number of fractional bits.</parameter>
        <parameter id="N">Total number of bits (integer + fractional).</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <signal id="sign_a" type="wire">Sign of input a.</signal>
        <signal id="sign_b" type="wire">Sign of input b.</signal>
        <signal id="abs_a" type="wire">Absolute value of input a.</signal>
        <signal id="abs_b" type="wire">Absolute value of input b.</signal>
        <signal id="res" type="wire">Result of the subtraction.</signal>
        <signal id="carry_out" type="wire">Carry out from the subtraction.</signal>
        <signal id="result_sign" type="wire">Sign of the result.</signal>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Extract signs
        assign sign_a = a[N-1];
        assign sign_b = b[N-1];

        // Calculate absolute values
        assign abs_a = sign_a ? ~a + 1 : a;
        assign abs_b = sign_b ? ~b + 1 : b;

        // Perform subtraction based on signs
        if (sign_a == sign_b) begin
            assign {carry_out, res} = abs_a - abs_b;
        end else begin
            assign {carry_out, res} = abs_a + abs_b;
        end

        // Determine result sign
        assign result_sign = (sign_a == sign_b) ? sign_a : (abs_a > abs_b);

        // Apply result sign
        assign c = {result_sign, res};

        // Handle zero case
        assign c = (res == 0) ? {N{1'b0}} : c;
    </implementation>
</module>

module up_down_counter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire up_down,
    output reg [15:0] count
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin
        count <= 16'b0;
    end else begin
        if (up_down) begin
            count <= count + 1;
        end else begin
            count <= count - 1;
        end
    end
end

endmodule

<module id="counter_12">
    <description>Counter from 4'b0000 to 4'd11, controlled by valid_count.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset.</input>
        <input id="clk">Clock.</input>
        <input id="valid_count">Signal to enable counting.</input>
        <output id="out" width_description="[3:0]">Current count.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="MAX_COUNT" value="4'd11"/>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="count_reg" width="4">Current count value.</register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                count_reg <= 4'b0000;
            end else if (valid_count) begin
                if (count_reg == MAX_COUNT) begin
                    count_reg <= 4'b0000;
                end else begin
                    count_reg <= count_reg + 1;
                end
            end
        end
        out <= count_reg;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="calendar">
    <description>Perpetual calendar module updating seconds, minutes, and hours.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="CLK">Clock input.</input>
        <input id="RST">Active-high reset signal.</input>
        <output id="Hours" width_description="[5:0]">6-bit output representing the current hours.</output>
        <output id="Mins" width_description="[5:0]">6-bit output representing the current minutes.</output>
        <output id="Secs" width_description="[5:0]">6-bit output representing the current seconds.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        reg [5:0] Secs;
        reg [5:0] Mins;
        reg [5:0] Hours;

        always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST) begin
            if (RST) begin
                Secs <= 6'd0;
                Mins <= 6'd0;
                Hours <= 6'd0;
            end else begin

    <description>4-bit BCD adder for decimal arithmetic operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[3:0]">First BCD input (4-bit).</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[3:0]">Second BCD input (4-bit).</input>
        <input id="Cin">Carry-in input (1-bit).</input>
        <output id="Sum" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit output representing the sum of the two BCD inputs, corrected to be a valid BCD digit (0–9).</output>
        <output id="Cout">Carry-out output (1-bit).</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Perform binary addition of A, B, and Cin
        reg [3:0] sum;
        reg cout;

        always @(*) begin
            sum = A + B + Cin;
            cout = (sum > 9);
            if (sum > 9) begin
                sum = sum + 6;
            end
        end

        // Assign outputs
        Sum = sum;
        Cout = cout;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="adder_32bit">
    <description>Implement a 32-bit carry-lookahead adder using the Carry-Lookahead Adder (CLA) architecture.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit input operand A.</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit input operand B.</input>
        <output id="S" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit output representing the sum of A and B.</output>
        <output id="C32">Carry-out output.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        <!-- Implement the 32-bit carry-lookahead adder using two 16-bit CLA blocks -->
        // Define the 16-bit CLA block
        function [15:0] cla_16;
            input [15:0] a, b, cin;
            begin
                wire [15:0] g, p, s;
                wire [14:0] c;

                // Generate and propagate signals
                for (integer i = 0; i <= 14; i = i + 1) begin : generate_propagate_generate
                    assign g[i] = a[i] & b[i];
                    assign p[i] = a[i] | b[i];
                end

                // Propagate signal
                assign c[0] = cin;
                for (integer i = 1; i <= 14; i = i + 1) begin : propagate_signal
                    assign c[i] = c[i - 1] | p[i - 1];
                end

                // Sum signal
                assign s[0] = a[0] ^ b[0] ^ cin;
                for (integer i = 1; i <= 15; i = i + 1) begin : sum_signal
                    assign s[i] = a[i] ^ b[i] ^ c[i - 1];
                end

                cla_16 = {c[14], s};
            end
        endfunction

        // Instantiate two 16-bit CLA blocks
        wire [15:0] s16, c16;
        wire [15:0] s32, c32;

        assign {s16, c16} = cla_16(A[15:0], B[15:0], A[16]);
        assign {s32, c32} = cla_16(s16, B[31:16], c16);

        // Combine results
        assign S = {c32, s32};
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="signal_generator">
    <description>Generates a triangle wave signal by incrementing and decrementing a 5-bit signal named 'wave'.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <output id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">5-bit output waveform signal representing the generated waveform.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="INCREMENT">0</parameter>
        <parameter name="DECREMENT">1</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        reg [4:0] wave;
        reg [1:0] state;

        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                wave <= 5'b00000;
                state <= INCREMENT;
            end else begin
                case (state)
                    INCREMENT: begin
                        if (wave == 5'b11111) begin
                            state <= DECREMENT;
                        end else begin
                            wave <= wave + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    DECREMENT: begin
                        if (wave == 5'b00000) begin
                            state <= INCREMENT;
                        end else begin
                            wave <= wave - 1;
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Generates a triangle wave by incrementing and decrementing a 5-bit signal.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="parallel2serial">
    <description>Parallel-to-serial converter where every four input bits are converted to a serial one bit output (MSB to LSB).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="d" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit parallel data input.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Valid signal indicating the availability of serial output.</output>
        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="IDLE"/>
        <parameter name="DATA_SHIFT"/>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width="2">Counter register.</reg>
        <reg id="data" width="4">Data register.</reg>
        <wire id="valid">Valid signal.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 2'b00;
                data <= 4'b0000;
                valid <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                case (cnt)
                    2'b00: begin
                        dout <= data[3];
                        valid <= 1'b1;
                        cnt <= 2'b01;
                    end
                    2'b01: begin
                        dout <= data[2];
                        valid <= 1'b1;
                        cnt <= 2'b10;
                    end
                    2'b10: begin
                        dout <= data[1];
                        valid <= 1'b1;
                        cnt <= 2'b11;
                    end
                    2'b11: begin
                        dout <= data[0];
                        valid <= 1'b1;
                        cnt <= 2'b00;
                    end
                    default: begin
                        cnt <= 2'b00;
                        data <= 4'b0000;
                        valid <= 1'b0;
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Unsigned 8-bit multiplier implemented with pipelining.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal that controls the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating if the multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH">8</parameter>
        <parameter id="PRODUCT_WIDTH">16</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="mul_en_out_reg" width="1" description="Register to hold the output enable signal."/>
        <register id="mul_a_reg" width="8" description="Register to hold the multiplicand."/>
        <register id="mul_b_reg" width="8" description="Register to hold the multiplier."/>
        <wire id="temp" width="8" description="Wire to hold partial products."/>
        <register id="sum" width="9" description="Register to hold intermediate sum values."/>
        <register id="mul_out_reg" width="16" description="Register to hold the final product."/>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_en_out_reg <= 1'b0;
                mul_a_reg <= 8'b0;
                mul_b_reg <= 8'b0;
                sum <= 9'b0;
                mul_out_reg <= 16'b0;
            end else begin
                if (mul_en_in) begin
                    mul_en_out_reg <= 1'b1;
                    mul_a_reg <= mul_a;
                    mul_b_reg <= mul_b;
                end else begin
                    mul_en_out_reg <= 1'b0;
                end

                for (integer i = 0; i < WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin
                    temp[i] <= mul_a_reg & (mul_b_reg >> i);
                end

                sum <= 9'b0;
                for (integer j = 0; j < WIDTH; j = j + 1) begin
                    sum <= sum + {temp[j], 1'b0};
                end

                mul_out_reg <= sum[15:0];
            end
        end

        assign mul_en_out = mul_en_out_reg;
        assign mul_out = mul_en_out_reg ? mul_out_reg : 16'b0;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="clkgenerator">
    <description>Generates a periodic clock signal with a period defined by the PERIOD parameter.</description>
    <ports>
        <output id="clk">The output clock signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="PERIOD">10</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        reg clk;
        integer counter;

        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                clk <= 0;
                counter <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (counter == PERIOD/2 - 1) begin
                    clk <= ~clk;
                    counter <= 0;
                end else begin
                    counter <= counter + 1;
                end
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Initializes the clock signal to 0. Toggles the clock every half of the specified PERIOD.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="ring_counter">
    <description>8-bit ring counter with cyclic state sequences.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal that drives the state transitions of the ring counter.</input>
        <input id="reset">Reset signal to initialize the counter to its starting state.</input>
        <output id="out" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit output representing the current state of the ring counter. Only one bit is set high at any time, and the set bit cycles through the 8-bit output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter>INITIAL_STATE = 8'b0000_0001</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        reg [7:0] counter;
        
        always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
            if (reset) begin
                counter <= INITIAL_STATE;
            end else begin
                counter <= {counter[6:0], counter[7]};
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>On each rising edge of the clock, the 1 shifts to the next bit in the sequence, wrapping around to the LSB after the MSB.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="freq_divbyfrac">
    <description>Fractional frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency by 3.5 using double-edge clocking technique.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Input clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active low reset signal to initialize the module.</input>
        <output id="clk_div">Fractionally divided clock output.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        Counter cycles through 7 clock cycles (MUL2_DIV_CLK = 7). Generates two uneven clock periods: one with 4 source clock cycles and another with 3 source clock cycles. In the next cycle, phase-shifted versions of the divided clock are generated. One phase is delayed by half a clock period, and the other is advanced by half a clock period. Finally, the two intermediate clocks are logically OR-ed to produce the final fractional divided clock output, ensuring the divided clock signal has a uniform period.
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="freq_diveven">
    <description>Frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency by even numbers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Input clock signal that will be divided.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal to initialize the module.</input>
        <output id="clk_div">Divided clock output signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="NUM_DIV">Even number specifying the division factor.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="cnt" width="4">Counter to track the number of clock cycles.</register>
        <wire id="half_num_div" width="4">Half of NUM_DIV.</wire>
        <wire id="toggle_clk_div" width="1">Signal to toggle clk_div.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Initialize counter and clk_div on reset
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 4'b0000;
                clk_div <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                // Calculate half of NUM_DIV
                half_num_div = NUM_DIV >> 1;
                
                // Check if counter has reached the limit
                if (cnt == half_num_div - 1) begin
                    cnt <= 4'b0000;
                    toggle_clk_div <= ~clk_div;
                end else begin
                    cnt <= cnt + 1'b1;
                    toggle_clk_div <= clk_div;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter>RESET</parameter>
        <parameter>LOAD</parameter>
        <parameter>MULTIPLY</parameter>
        <parameter>READY</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="multiplier" width="16">Multiplier register.</reg>
        <reg id="multiplicand" width="16">Multiplicand register.</reg>
        <reg id="product" width="16">Product register.</reg>
        <reg id="ctr" width="5">Counter register.</reg>
        <wire id="ready_flag">Ready flag.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
            if (reset) begin
                multiplier <= {8{a[7]}, a};
                multiplicand <= {8{b[7]}, b};
                product <= 16'b0;
                ctr <= 5'b0;
                ready_flag <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                case (ctr)
                    5'b0: begin
                        // Load initial values
                        multiplier <= {8{a[7]}, a};
                        multiplicand <= {8{b[7]}, b};
                        product <= 16'b0;
                        ctr <= 5'b1;
                    end
                    5'b16: begin
                        // Multiplication complete
                        ready_flag <= 1'b1;
                    end
                    default: begin
                        // Booth algorithm steps
                        if (multiplier[ctr] == 1'b1) begin
                            product <= product + multiplicand;
                        end
                        multiplicand <= {multiplicand[14:0], 1'b0}; // Left shift multiplicand
                        ctr <= ctr + 1'b1;
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
        assign rdy = ready_flag;
    </implementation>

<module id="multi_pipe_4bit">
    <description>4-bit unsigned number pipeline multiplier with two levels of registers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit input multiplicand.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit input multiplier.</input>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit product output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="size" value="4">Size of the input and output operands.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <reg type="sequential_logic" id="partial_product" width="4">Register to store partial products.</reg>
        <reg type="sequential_logic" id="accumulator" width="8">Register to accumulate partial sums.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Extension of input signals
        wire [7:0] extended_mul_a = {mul_a, 2'b00};
        wire [7:0] extended_mul_b = {mul_b, 2'b00};

        // Generate block to calculate partial products
        generate
            for (genvar i = 0; i < size; i++) begin : partial_product_gen
                assign partial_product[i] = (extended_mul_b[i]) ? (extended_mul_a << i) : 4'b0;
            end
        endgenerate

        // Register to store intermediate sum values
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                accumulator <= 8'b0;
            end else begin
                accumulator <= accumulator + {partial_product[0], partial_product[1], partial_product[2], partial_product[3]};
            end
        end

        // Final product calculation
        assign mul_out = accumulator;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="barrel_shifter">
    <description>A barrel shifter for rotating bits efficiently. This 8-bit barrel shifter takes an 8-bit input and shifts or rotates the bits based on a 3-bit control signal.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="in" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input to be shifted.</input>
        <input id="ctrl" width_description="[2:0]">3-bit control signal that determines how many positions to shift.</input>
        <output id="out" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit shifted output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <!-- No parameter_description needed for this example -->
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <!-- Sequential logic for the barrel shifter -->
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Barrel Shifter Logic
        wire [7:0] shifted_by_4;
        wire [7:0] shifted_by_2;
        wire [7:0] shifted_by_1;

        // Shift by 4 positions
        assign shifted_by_4 = {in[3:0], in[7:4]};

        // Shift by 2 positions
        assign shifted_by_2 = {in[1:0], in[7:2]};

        // Shift by 1 position
        assign shifted_by_1 = {in[0], in[7:1]};

        // Final output based on ctrl signal
        assign out = (ctrl == 3'b001) ? shifted_by_1 :
                   (ctrl == 3'b010) ? shifted_by_2 :
                   (ctrl == 3'b100) ? shifted_by_4 :
                   in; // Default to original input if ctrl is 000
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="synchronizer">
    <description>A multi-bit MUX-based synchronizer that ensures data remains constant during data_en high periods and synchronizes it across two clocks.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk_a" width_description="">Clock signal A used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="clk_b" width_description="">Clock signal B used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="arstn" width_description="">Active-low reset signal A. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="brstn" width_description="">Active-low reset signal B. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[3:0]">Input data signal of size 4 bits.</input>
        <input id="data_en" width_description="">Input enable signal that controls the selection operation.</input>
        <output id="dataout" width_description="[3:0]">Output data signal of size 4 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description></parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="data_reg" width_description="[3:0]" type="register">Register to store the input data signal.</reg>
        <reg id="en_data_reg" width_description="" type="register">Register to store the input enable signal.</reg>
        <reg id="en_clap_one" width_description="" type="register">First enable control register.</reg>
        <reg id="en_clap_two" width_description="" type="register">Second enable control register.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Data Register Update
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (!arstn) begin
                data_reg <= 4'b0;
            end else begin
                if (data_en) begin
                    data_reg <= data_in;
                end
            end
        end

        // Enable Data Register Update
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (!arstn) begin
                en_data_reg <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                en_data_reg <= data_en;
            end
        end

        // Enable Control Registers Update
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (!brstn) begin
                en_clap_one <= 1'b0;
                en_clap_two <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                en_clap_one <= en_data_reg;
                en_clap_two <= en_clap_one;
            end
        end

        // Output Assignment
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (!brstn) begin
                dataout <= 4'b0;
            end else begin
                if (en_clap_two) begin
                    dataout <= data_reg;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="pulse_detect">
    <description>Detects pulses in a 1-bit input signal data_in. A pulse is defined as a sequence of 0 to 1 to 0 over three cycles. The output signal data_out indicates the end of a pulse.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="data_in">One-bit input signal.</input>
        <output id="data_out">Output signal indicating the presence of pulses.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="IDLE">Idle state.</parameter>
        <parameter name="RISING">Rising edge detected.</parameter>
        <parameter name="FALLING">Falling edge detected.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="state" type="reg" width="2">State register.</register>
        <wire id="next_state" type="wire" width="2">Next state wire.</wire>
        <wire id="data_out_reg" type="wire">Data out register.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                state <= IDLE;
                data_out_reg <= 0;
            end else begin
                case (state)
                    IDLE: begin
                        if (data_in == 1'b0) begin
                            next_state = RISING;
                        end else begin
                            next_state = IDLE;
                        end
                    end
                    RISING: begin
                        if (data_in == 1'b1) begin
                            next_state = FALLING;
                        end else begin
                            next_state = IDLE;
                        end
                    end
                    FALLING: begin
                        if (data_in == 1'b0) begin
                            next_state = IDLE;
                            data_out_reg = 1;
                        end else begin
                            next_state = RISING;
                        end
                    end
                endcase
                state <= next_state;
            end
        end
        data_out <= data_out_reg;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="fsm">
    <description>Detection circuit for a specific sequence '10011' in a continuous input stream. Outputs MATCH=1 when the sequence is detected.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="IN" width_description="">Single-bit input signal.</input>
        <input id="CLK">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="RST">Reset signal to initialize the FSM.</input>
        <output id="MATCH" width_description="">Output signal indicating a match condition.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter>STATE_IDLE</parameter>
        <parameter>STATE_1</parameter>
        <parameter>STATE_2</parameter>
        <parameter>STATE_3</parameter>
        <parameter>STATE_4</parameter>
        <parameter>STATE_MATCH</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="current_state" width_description="3">Current state of the FSM.</reg>
        <wire id="next_state" width_description="3">Next state of the FSM.</wire>
        <wire id="match_condition" width_description="">Intermediate signal to check match condition.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // State encoding
        parameter STATE_IDLE = 3'b000;
        parameter STATE_1 = 3'b001;
        parameter STATE_2 = 3'b010;
        parameter STATE_3 = 3'b011;
        parameter STATE_4 = 3'b100;
        parameter STATE_MATCH = 3'b101;

        // Next state logic
        always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST) begin
            if (RST) begin
                current_state <= STATE_IDLE;
            end else begin
                current_state <= next_state;
            end
        end

        // Match condition logic
        assign match_condition = (current_state == STATE_4 && IN == 1);

        // Output logic
        assign MATCH = match_condition;

        // Next state determination
        always @(*) begin
            case (current_state)
                STATE_IDLE: begin
                    if (IN == 1) next_state = STATE_1;
                    else next_state = STATE_IDLE;
                end
                STATE_1: begin
                    if (IN == 0) next_state = STATE_2;
                    else next_state = STATE_IDLE;
                end
                STATE_2: begin
                    if (IN == 0) next_state = STATE_3;
                    else next_state = STATE_IDLE;
                end
                STATE_3: begin
                    if (IN == 1) next_state = STATE_4;
                    else next_state = STATE_IDLE;
                end
                STATE_4: begin
                    if (IN == 1) next_state = STATE_MATCH;
                    else next_state = STATE_IDLE;
                end
                STATE_MATCH: begin
                    next_state = STATE_IDLE;
                end
                default: begin
                    next_state = STATE_IDLE;
                end
            endcase
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="freq_divbyodd">
    <description>A frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency by an odd number provided as a parameter.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Input clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active low reset signal that initializes the divider.</input>
        <output id="clk_div">Divided clock output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="NUM_DIV" default_value="5">Odd divisor value for clock division.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt1" width="log2(NUM_DIV)">Counter for rising edge.</reg>
        <reg id="cnt2" width="log2(NUM_DIV)">Counter for falling edge.</reg>
        <wire id="clk_div1">Clock divider for positive edge.</wire>
        <wire id="clk_div2">Clock divider for negative edge.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt1 <= 0;
                cnt2 <= 0;
                clk_div1 <= 0;
                clk_div2 <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt1 == (NUM_DIV / 2)) begin
                    clk_div1 <= ~clk_div1;
                    cnt1 <= 0;
                end else begin
                    cnt1 <= cnt1 + 1;
                end

                if (cnt2 == (NUM_DIV / 2)) begin
                    clk_div2 <= ~clk_div2;
                    cnt2 <= 0;
                end else begin
                    cnt2 <= cnt2 + 1;
                end
            end
        end

        assign clk_div = clk_div1 | clk_div2;
    </implementation>
</module>

        <input id="dataIn" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit input data to be pushed onto the buffer.</input>
        <input id="RW">Read/Write control signal (1 for read, 0 for write).</input>
        <input id="EN">Enable signal to activate buffer operations.</input>
        <input id="Rst">Active high reset signal to initialize the buffer.</input>
        <input id="Clk">Clock signal for synchronous operations.</input>
        <output id="EMPTY">Flag indicating whether the buffer is empty.</output>
        <output id="FULL">Flag indicating whether the buffer is full.</output>
        <output id="dataOut" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit output data retrieved from the buffer.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="EMPTY">Buffer is empty.</parameter>
        <parameter name="FULL">Buffer is full.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="stack_mem" width="4" depth="4">Stack memory array to store the data.</reg>
        <reg id="SP" width="2">Stack pointer tracking the current position in the stack.</reg>
        <wire id="EMPTY_flag">Flag indicating whether the buffer is empty.</wire>
        <wire id="FULL_flag">Flag indicating whether the buffer is full.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge Clk) begin
            if (Rst) begin
                SP <= 4;
                stack_mem <= {4{4'b0}};
                EMPTY_flag <= 1'b1;
                FULL_flag <= 1'b0;
            end else if (EN) begin
                if (RW == 1'b0 && !FULL_flag) begin
                    stack_mem[SP] <= dataIn;
                    SP <= SP + 1;
                end else if (RW == 1'b1 && !EMPTY_flag) begin
                    dataOut <= stack_mem[SP];
                    stack_mem[SP] <= 4'b0;
                    SP <= SP - 1;
                end
            end
        end
        EMPTY <= (SP == 4);
        FULL <= (SP == 0);
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="alu">
    <description>ALU for a 32-bit MIPS-ISA CPU.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit input operand A.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit input operand B.</input>
        <input id="aluc" width_description="[5:0]">6-bit control signal for selecting the operation to be performed.</input>
        <output id="r" width_description="[31:0]">32-bit output representing the result of the operation.</output>
        <output id="zero">1-bit output indicating whether the result is zero.</output>
        <output id="carry">1-bit output indicating whether a carry occurred during the operation.</output>
        <output id="negative">1-bit output indicating whether the result is negative.</output>
        <output id="overflow">1-bit output indicating whether an overflow occurred during the operation.</output>
        <output id="flag">1-bit output representing a general flag, which is set based on specific operations (SLT and SLTU).</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="ADD">6'b100000</parameter>
        <parameter name="ADDU">6'b100001</parameter>
        <parameter name="SUB">6'b100010</parameter>
        <parameter name="SUBU">6'b100011</parameter>
        <parameter name="AND">6'b100100</parameter>
        <parameter name="OR">6'b100101</parameter>
        <parameter name="XOR">6'b100110</parameter>
        <parameter name="NOR">6'b100111</parameter>
        <parameter name="SLT">6'b101010</parameter>
        <parameter name="SLTU">6'b101011</parameter>
        <parameter name="SLL">6'b000000</parameter>
        <parameter name="SRL">6'b000010</parameter>
        <parameter name="SRA">6'b000011</parameter>
        <parameter name="SLLV">6'b000100</parameter>
        <parameter name="SRLV">6'b000110</parameter>
        <parameter name="SRAV">6'b000111</parameter>
        <parameter name="LUI">6'b001111</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <signal id="res" width_description="[63:0]" type="wire">Result register.</signal>
        <signal id="shift_amount" width_description="[4:0]" type="wire">Shift amount.</signal>
        <signal id="signed_a" width_description="[31:0]" type="wire">Signed version of a.</signal>
        <signal id="signed_b" width_description="[31:0]" type="wire">Signed version of b.</signal>
        <assign>signed_a = $signed(a);</assign>
        <assign>signed_b = $signed(b);</assign>
        <always @(*)>
            case (aluc)
                ADD: res = signed_a + signed_b;
                ADDU: res = a + b;
                SUB: res = signed_a - signed_b;
                SUBU: res = a - b;
                AND: res = a & b;
                OR: res = a | b;
                XOR: res = a ^ b;
                NOR: res = ~(a | b);
                SLT: begin
                    res = {31{signed_a[31]}};
                    if (signed_a < signed_b) res[0] = 1'b1;
                end
                SLTU: begin
                    res = {31{a[31]}};
                    if (a < b) res[0] = 1'b1;
                end
                SLL: begin
                    shift_amount = a[4:0];
                    res = {a << shift_amount, {32{a[31]}}};
                end
                SRL: begin
                    shift_amount = a[4:0];
                    res = {a >> shift_amount, {32{a[31]}}};
                end
                SRA: begin
                    shift_amount = a[4:0];
                    res = {a >>> shift_amount, {32{a[31]}}};
                end
                SLLV: begin
                    shift_amount = a[4:0];
                    res = {a << shift_amount, {32{a[31]}}};
                end
                SRLV: begin
                    shift_amount = a[4:0];
                    res = {a >> shift_amount, {32{a[31]}}};
                end
                SRAV: begin
                    shift_amount = a[4:0];
                    res = {a >>> shift_amount, {32{a[31]}}};
                end
                LUI: res = {a[15:0], 16'd0};
                default: res = {64{1'bz}};
            endcase
        </always>
        <assign>r = res[31:0];</assign>
        <assign>zero = (r == 32'd0) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;</assign>
        <assign>carry = (aluc == ADD || aluc == SUB) ? (res[32] != signed_a[31]) : 1'b0;</assign>
        <assign>negative = (r[31] == 1'b1) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;</assign>
        <assign>overflow = ((aluc == ADD || aluc == SUB) && (signed_a[31] == signed_b[31]) && (signed_a[31] != res[31])) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;</assign>
        <assign>flag = (aluc == SLT || aluc == SLTU) ? (res[0] == 1'b1) : 1'bz;</assign>
    </logic_description>
</module>

<module id="sequence_detector">
    <description>Sequence Detector to detect the 4-bit binary sequence 1001.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal to synchronize the detector.</input>
        <input id="reset_n">Active-low reset signal to initialize the state machine.</input>
        <input id="data_in">1-bit binary input signal to feed the bitstream for sequence detection.</input>
        <output id="sequence_detected">1-bit output signal that is set high when the specific sequence is detected.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter>IDLE</parameter>
        <parameter>S1</parameter>
        <parameter>S2</parameter>
        <parameter>S3</parameter>
        <parameter>S4</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="current_state" width_description="[2:0]">Current state of the FSM.</register>
        <wire id="next_state" width_description="[2:0]">Next state of the FSM.</wire>
        <wire id="match_s1" width="1">Match with the first bit of the sequence.</wire>
        <wire id="match_s2" width="1">Match with the second bit of the sequence.</wire>
        <wire id="match_s3" width="1">Match with the third bit of the sequence.</wire>
        <wire id="match_s4" width="1">Match with the fourth bit of the sequence.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // State transition logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
            if (!reset_n) begin
                current_state <= 3'b000; // IDLE
            end else begin
                current_state <= next_state;
            end
        end

        // Next state logic
        always @(*) begin
            case (current_state)
                3'b000: // IDLE
                    if (data_in == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = 3'b001; // S1
                    end else begin
                        next_state = 3'b000; // IDLE
                    end
                3'b001: // S1
                    if (data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = 3'b010; // S2
                    end else begin
                        next_state = 3'b000; // IDLE
                    end
                3'b010: // S2
                    if (data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = 3'b011; // S3
                    end else begin
                        next_state = 3'b000; // IDLE
                    end
                3'b011: // S3
                    if (data_in == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = 3'b100; // S4
                    end else begin
                        next_state = 3'b000; // IDLE
                    end
                3'b100: // S4
                    next_state = 3'b000; // IDLE
                default:
                    next_state = 3'b000; // IDLE
            endcase
        end

        // Output logic
        always @(*) begin
            sequence_detected = 1'b0;
            case (current_state)
                3'b100: // S4
                    sequence_detected = 1'b1;
                default:
                    sequence_detected = 1'b0;
            endcase
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="JC_counter">
    <description>64-bit Johnson counter (torsional ring counter).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal to initialize the counter.</input>
        <output id="Q" width_description="[63:0]">64-bit register representing the current count value.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>On every rising edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the counter value is updated. If the reset signal (rst_n) is low, indicating a reset condition, the counter value (Q) is set to 0. Otherwise, if the least significant bit (Q[0]) is 0, the counter increments by shifting the current value (Q[63:1]) to the right and appending a 1 at the most significant bit position. If the least significant bit (Q[0]) is 1, the counter decrements by shifting the current value (Q[63:1]) to the right and appending a 0 at the most significant bit position.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="adder_pipe_64bit">
    <description>64-bit ripple carry adder with pipelining stages.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock input.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="i_en">Enable signal for addition operation.</input>
        <input id="adda" width_description="[63:0]">64-bit input operand A.</input>
        <input id="addb" width_description="[63:0]">64-bit input operand B.</input>
        <output id="result" width_description="[64:0]">65-bit output representing the sum of adda and addb.</output>
        <output id="o_en">Output enable signal indicating the availability of the result.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="IDLE">Idle state.</parameter>
        <parameter name="ADD">Addition state.</parameter>
        <parameter name="RESULT">Result state.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="current_state" width="2">Current state of the FSM.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" width="2">Next state of the FSM.</reg>
        <reg id="pipe_adda" width="64">Pipelined input operand A.</reg>
        <reg id="pipe_addb" width="64">Pipelined input operand B.</reg>
        <reg id="pipe_carry_in" width="1">Pipelined carry-in signal.</reg>
        <reg id="pipe_sum" width="65">Pipelined sum value.</reg>
        <wire id="sum" width="65">Sum value calculated during addition.</wire>
        <wire id="carry_out" width="1">Carry-out signal from the last adder.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // State transition logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                current_state <= IDLE;
            end else begin
                current_state <= next_state;
            end
        end

        // Next state logic
        always @(*) begin
            case (current_state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (i_en) begin
                        next_state = ADD;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = IDLE;
                    end
                end
                ADD: begin
                    next_state = RESULT;
                end
                RESULT: begin
                    next_state = IDLE;
                end
                default: begin
                    next_state = IDLE;
                end
            endcase
        end

        // Pipeline register updates
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                pipe_adda <= 64'b0;
                pipe_addb <= 64'b0;
                pipe_carry_in <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (current_state == IDLE && i_en) begin
                    pipe_adda <= adda;
                    pipe_addb <= addb;
                    pipe_carry_in <= 1'b0;
                end
            end
        end

        // Addition logic
        assign sum = $unsigned(pipe_adda) + $unsigned(pipe_addb) + pipe_carry_in;

        // Carry-out calculation
        generate
            genvar i;
            for (i = 0; i < 64; i = i + 1) begin : adders
                assign carry_out = |(sum[i+1:i]);
            end
        endgenerate

        // Result register update
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                pipe_sum <= 65'b0;
            end else begin
                if (current_state == RESULT) begin
                    pipe_sum <= {carry_out, sum};
                end
            end
        end

        // Output enable logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                o_en <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (current_state == RESULT) begin
                    o_en <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    o_en <= 1'b0;
                end
            end
        end

        // Final result assignment
        assign result = pipe_sum;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="traffic_light">
    <description>A traffic light controller with red, yellow, and green indicators, and a pedestrian button.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset.</input>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="pass_request">Request signal for pedestrians.</input>
        <output id="clock" width_description="[7:0]">An 8-bit output representing the count value of the internal counter.</output>
        <output id="red">Red light output.</output>
        <output id="yellow">Yellow light output.</output>
        <output id="green">Green light output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="idle">Idle state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s1_red">State 1: Red.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s2_yellow">State 2: Yellow.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s3_green">State 3: Green.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <register id="cnt" type="sequential_logic">Internal counter for timing.</register>
        <register id="state" type="sequential_logic">Current state of the traffic light controller.</register>
        <register id="p_red" type="sequential_logic">Previous value of red signal.</register>
        <register id="p_yellow" type="sequential_logic">Previous value of yellow signal.</register>
        <register id="p_green" type="sequential_logic">Previous value of green signal.</register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // State transition logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                state <= s1_red;
                cnt <= 8'd10;
                p_red <= 1'b0;
                p_yellow <= 1'b0;
                p_green <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                case (state)
                    s1_red: begin
                        if (cnt == 8'd3) begin
                            state <= s3_green;
                            cnt <= 8'd60;
                        end else begin
                            cnt <= cnt - 1;
                        end
                    end
                    s2_yellow: begin
                        if (cnt == 8'd3) begin
                            state <= s1_red;
                            cnt <= 8'd5;
                        end else begin
                            cnt <= cnt - 1;
                        end
                    end
                    s3_green: begin
                        if (cnt == 8'd3) begin
                            state <= s2_yellow;
                            cnt <= 8'd10;
                        end else begin
                            cnt <= cnt - 1;
                        end
                    end
                    default: state <= s1_red;
                endcase
            end
        end

        // Counting logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 8'd10;
            end else if (pass_request && p_green) begin
                cnt <= 8'd10;
            end else if (!p_green && p_green == 1'b1) begin
                cnt <= 8'd60;
            end else if (!p_yellow && p_yellow == 1'b1) begin
                cnt <= 8'd5;
            end else if (!p_red && p_red == 1'b1) begin
                cnt <= 8'd10;
            end else begin
                cnt <= cnt - 1;
            end
        end

        // Output assignment
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                red <= 1'b0;
                yellow <= 1'b0;
                green <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                p_red <= red;
                p_yellow <= yellow;
                p_green <= green;
                red <= ~green & ~yellow;
                yellow <= ~green & ~red;
                green <= ~red & ~yellow;
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="radix2_div">
    <description>Implement a simplified radix-2 divider on 8-bit signed or unsigned integers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst">The reset signal to initialize or reset the module.</input>
        <input id="sign">1-bit indicates if the operation is signed (1) or unsigned (0).</input>
        <input id="dividend" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input signal representing the dividend for division.</input>
        <input id="divisor" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input signal representing the divisor for division.</input>
        <input id="opn_valid">1-bit indicates that a valid operation request is present.</input>
        <output id="res_valid">1-bit output signal indicating the result is valid and ready.</output>
        <output id="result" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit the output containing the remainder in the upper 8 bits and the quotient in the lower 8 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="DIV_WIDTH">8</parameter>
        <parameter id="RES_WIDTH">16</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="SR" width="9">Shift Register.</reg>
        <reg id="NEG_DIVISOR" width="9">Negated Divisor.</reg>
        <reg id="cnt" width="4">Counter.</reg>
        <reg id="start_cnt" width="1">Start Counter Flag.</reg>
        <reg id="quotient" width="8">Quotient.</reg>
        <reg id="remainder" width="8">Remainder.</reg>
        <wire id="sub_result" width="9">Subtraction Result.</wire>
        <wire id="carry_out" width="1">Carry-Out.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
            if (rst) begin
                SR <= {1'b0, dividend};
                NEG_DIVISOR <= {1'b0, ~divisor + 1};
                cnt <= 4'd0;
                start_cnt <= 1'b0;
                quotient <= 8'd0;
                remainder <= 8'd0;
                res_valid <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (opn_valid && !res_valid) begin
                    SR <= {1'b0, dividend};
                    NEG_DIVISOR <= {1'b0, ~divisor + 1};
                    cnt <= 4'd1;
                    start_cnt <= 1'b1;
                end

                if (start_cnt) begin
                    if (cnt == 4'd8) begin
                        quotient <= SR[7:0];
                        remainder <= SR[15:8];
                        cnt <= 4'd0;
                        start_cnt <= 1'b0;
                        res_valid <= 1'b1;

<module id="accu">
    <description>Accumulates 4 input 8-bit data and outputs the sum along with a valid signal.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock input for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input data for addition.</input>
        <input id="valid_in">Input signal indicating readiness for new data.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Output signal indicating when 4 input data accumulation is reached.</output>
        <output id="data_out" width_description="[9:0]">10-bit output data representing the accumulated sum.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="NUM_DATA">4</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="count">4-bit register to count the number of valid inputs received.</reg>
        <reg id="accumulated_sum">10-bit register to store the accumulated sum.</reg>
        <wire id="new_data_valid">Wire to indicate if new data is valid.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                count <= 4'b0;
                accumulated_sum <= 10'b0;
                valid_out <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (valid_in && count < NUM_DATA) begin
                    accumulated_sum <= accumulated_sum + data_in;
                    count <= count + 1'b1;
                end
                if (count == NUM_DATA) begin
                    valid_out <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    valid_out <= 1'b0;
                end
            end
        end
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                data_out <= 10'b0;
            end else begin
                if (valid_out) begin
                    data_out <= accumulated_sum;
                end else begin
                    data_out <= 10'b0;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="float_multi">
    <description>32-bit floating-point multiplier for IEEE-754 standard single-precision arithmetic.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="rst">Reset signal (active high).</input>
        <input id="a" width_description="[31:0]">First operand in IEEE 754 format.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[31:0]">Second operand in IEEE 754 format.</input>
        <output id="z" width_description="[31:0]">Result of the multiplication in IEEE 754 format.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="IDLE"/>
        <parameter name="EXTRACT"/>
        <parameter name="SPECIAL_CASE"/>
        <parameter name="NORMALIZE"/>
        <parameter name="MULTIPLY"/>
        <parameter name="ROUND_ADJUST"/>
        <parameter name="OUTPUT"/>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <signal id="counter" type="reg" width="3">Cycle counter for operation sequencing.</signal>
        <signal id="a_mantissa" type="reg" width="23">Mantissa of input number a.</signal>
        <signal id="b_mantissa" type="reg" width="23">Mantissa of input number b.</signal>
        <signal id="z_mantissa" type="reg" width="23">Mantissa of output number.</signal>
        <signal id="a_exponent" type="reg" width="9">Exponent of input number a.</signal>
        <signal id="b_exponent" type="reg" width="9">Exponent of input number b.</signal>
        <signal id="z_exponent" type="reg" width="9">Exponent of output number.</signal>
        <signal id="a_sign" type="reg">Sign bit of input number a.</signal>
        <signal id="b_sign" type="reg">Sign bit of input number b.</signal>
        <signal id="z_sign" type="reg">Sign bit of output number.</signal>
        <signal id="product" type="reg" width="49">Intermediate product of the mantissas.</signal>
        <signal id="guard_bit" type="reg">Guard bit for rounding.</signal>
        <signal id="round_bit" type="reg">Round bit for rounding.</signal>
        <signal id="sticky" type="reg">Sticky bit for rounding.</signal>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        Always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
            if (rst) begin
                counter <= 3'b000;
                a_mantissa <= 23'b0;
                b_mantissa <= 23'b0;
                z_mantissa <= 23'b0;
                a_exponent <= 9'b0;
                b_exponent <= 9'b0;
                z_exponent <= 9'b0;
                a_sign <= 1'b0;
                b_sign <= 1'b0;
                z_sign <= 1'b0;
                product <= 49'b0;
                guard_bit <= 1'b0;
                round_bit <= 1'b0;
                sticky <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                case (counter)
                    3'b000: // IDLE
                        // Extract mantissas, exponents, and sign bits
                        a_mantissa <= a[22:0];
                        b_mantissa <= b[22:0];
                        a_exponent <= a[30:23];
                        b_exponent <= b[30:23];
                        a_sign <= a[31];
                        b_sign <= b[31];
                        counter <= 3'b001;
                    3'b001: // EXTRACT
                        // Handle special cases (NaN, Infinity)
                        if ((a_exponent == 9'hFF && a_mantissa != 23'b0) || (b_exponent == 9'hFF && b_mantissa != 23'b0)) begin
                            counter <= 3'b010;
                        end else begin
                            counter <= 3'b011;
                        end
                    3'b010: // SPECIAL_CASE
                        // Set output to NaN or Infinity
                        z_mantissa <= 23'b11111111111111111111111;
                        z_exponent <= 9'hFF;
                        z_sign <= a_sign ^ b_sign;
                        counter <= 3'b100;
                    3'b011: // NORMALIZE
                        // Normalize mantissas if needed
                        if (a_mantissa[22] == 1'b0) begin
                            a_mantissa <= {a_mantissa[21:0], 1'b0};
                            a_exponent <= a_exponent - 1;
                        end
                        if (b_mantissa[22] == 1'b0) begin
                            b_mantissa <= {b_mantissa[21:0], 1'b0};
                            b_exponent <= b_exponent - 1;
                        end
                        counter <= 3'b101;
                    3'b101: // MULTIPLY
                        // Multiply mantissas
                        product <= $signed(a_mantissa) * $signed(b_mantissa);
                        z_exponent <= a_exponent + b_exponent - 127;
                        z_sign <= a_sign ^ b_sign;
                        counter <= 3'b110;
                    3'b110: // ROUND_ADJUST
                        // Round and adjust exponent
                        guard_bit <= product[48];
                        round_bit <= product[47];
                        sticky <= |product[46:0];
                        if (round_bit && (guard_bit || sticky)) begin
                            z_mantissa <= product[46:23] + 1;
                        end else begin
                            z_mantissa <= product[46:23];
                        end
                        if (z_mantissa[23] == 1'b1) begin
                            z_exponent <= z_exponent + 1;
                            z_mantissa <= z_mantissa >> 1;
                        end
                        counter <= 3'b111;
                    3'b111: // OUTPUT
                        // Format output in IEEE 754 standard
                        z <= {z_sign, z_exponent, z_mantissa};
                        counter <= 3'b000;
                endcase
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

    <description>Asynchronous FIFO with configurable depth and width.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="wclk">Write clock signal used for synchronous write operations.</input>
        <input id="rclk">Read clock signal used for synchronous read operations.</input>
        <input id="wrstn">Write reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="rrstn">Read reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="winc">Write increment signal. Used to trigger write operations.</input>
        <input id="rinc">Read increment signal. Used to trigger read operations.</input>
        <input id="wdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Write data input.</input>
        <output id="wfull">Write full signal. Indicates if the FIFO is full and cannot accept further write operations.</output>
        <output id="rempty">Read empty signal. Indicates if the FIFO is empty and cannot provide any data for read operations.</output>
        <output id="rdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Read data output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH">8</parameter>
        <parameter id="DEPTH">16</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <signal id="waddr_bin" type="reg" width_description="[${$clog2(DEPTH)}-1:0]">Write address register.</signal>
        <signal id="raddr_bin" type="reg" width_description="[${$clog2(DEPTH)}-1:0]">Read address register.</signal>
        <signal id="wptr" type="reg" width_description="[${$clog2(DEPTH)}-1:0]">Write pointer.</signal>
        <signal id="rptr" type="reg" width_description="[${$clog2(DEPTH)}-1:0]">Read pointer.</signal>
        <signal id="wptr_buff" type="reg" width_description="[${$clog2(DEPTH)}-1:0]">Write pointer buffer.</signal>
        <signal id="rptr_buff" type="reg" width_description="[${$clog2(DEPTH)}-1:0]">Read pointer buffer.</signal>
        <signal id="wen" type="wire">Write enable signal.</signal>
        <signal id="ren" type="wire">Read enable signal.</signal>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Dual-port RAM instantiation
        dual_port_RAM #(.WIDTH(WIDTH), .DEPTH(DEPTH)) dual_port_ram (
            .wclk(wclk),
            .renc(ren),
            .wenc(wen),
            .waddr(waddr_bin),
            .raddr(raddr_bin),
            .wdata(wdata),
            .rdata(rdata)
        );

        // Write pointer logic
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                waddr_bin <= 0;
                wptr <= 0;
            end else if (winc && !wfull) begin
                waddr_bin <= (waddr_bin + 1) % DEPTH;
                wptr <= (wptr + 1) % DEPTH;
            end
        end

        // Read pointer logic
        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                raddr_bin <= 0;
                rptr <= 0;
            end else if (rinc && !rempty) begin
                raddr_bin <= (raddr_bin + 1) % DEPTH;
                rptr <= (rptr + 1) % DEPTH;
            end
        end

        // Pointer buffers
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                wptr_buff <= 0;
            end else begin
                wptr_buff <= wptr;
            end
        end

        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                rptr_buff <= 0;
            end else begin
                rptr_buff <= rptr;
            end
        end

        // Full and empty signals
        assign wfull = (wptr == ((~rptr_buff << 1) | (rptr_buff & 4'b0011)));
        assign rempty = (rptr == wptr);
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="serial2parallel">
    <description>Serial-to-Parallel Conversion Circuit</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="din_serial">Serial input data.</input>
        <input id="din_valid">Validity signal for input data.</input>
        <output id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data (8 bits wide).</output>
        <output id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter name="IDLE">Idle state.</parameter>
        <parameter name="COUNTING">Counting state.</parameter>
        <parameter name="DATA_WIDTH">8</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width="4">4-bit counter to track the number of received bits.</reg>
        <reg id="dout_parallel_reg" width="8">Register to hold the parallel output data.</reg>
        <wire id="dout_valid_wire">Wire to hold the valid output signal.</wire>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 4'b0;
                dout_parallel_reg <= 8'b0;
                dout_valid_wire <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                if (din_valid && cnt < DATA_WIDTH) begin
                    dout_parallel_reg[cnt] <= din_serial;
                    cnt <= cnt + 1;
                end
                if (cnt == DATA_WIDTH) begin
                    dout_valid_wire <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    dout_valid_wire <= 1'b0;
                end
            end
        end
        assign dout_parallel = dout_parallel_reg;
        assign dout_valid = dout_valid_wire;
    </implementation>
</module>
